features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal relevant technical education or degree attainment the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no advanced degree signal.
Master's degree in a relevant technical field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems architecture
features.description: Direct design or ownership of agent-based systems, especially their orchestration, guardrails, and supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering problem-solving examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Collaborative learning mindset
features.description: Whether the letter presents the applicant as coachable and inclined to partner with security specialists or internal users rather than work purely solo.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear collaboration or internal-customer orientation.
Uses generic team language, but without a concrete sense of collaborators or users.
Explicitly mentions partnering with security engineers or serving developer teams.
Clearly frames success as collaborative enablement, including learning from specialists and building thoughtfully for other engineers.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Whether the letter frames security work as helping developers and internal users through better defaults, usable tooling, empathy, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Whether the letter signals a quality bar centered on reliability, correctness, maintenance, guardrails, and long-term operability.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How much the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, architecture details, or other specific evidence.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's professional production work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes, effects, or visible results of the applicant's work rather than only naming activities.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists duties or technologies with little sense of outcome.
Implies positive effect, but without a clear result.
States a clear before-and-after outcome for at least one contribution.
Shows vivid or quantified operational impact that explains what changed for the team.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: How well the letter forms a connected, structured story or argument instead of a disconnected list of claims.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a disconnected inventory of facts or a compliance-style form letter.
Has some stated motivation, but the link from prior work to this role is thin or mechanical.
Presents a coherent progression from prior experience to the target role.
Tells a memorable, well-shaped story that makes the move into this role feel natural, intentional, and earned.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Whether the letter has a memorable, individualized voice or framing rather than sounding generic or templated.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary software work, such as CTF participation or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Contribution to, maintenance of, or upstream repair in public codebases used beyond the applicant's immediate employer team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or fixes sent upstream.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintainership, including review or release responsibilities.
The letter shows stewardship of a broadly used project or community, with clear responsibility for releases, roadmap, or contributor management.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical scope, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed engineering work outside formal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The letter mentions only a small utility or simple personal app.
The letter shows a moderately technical side project with some nontrivial design.
The letter shows a substantial systems project with reliability or distributed-systems concerns.
The letter shows an unusually ambitious build from first principles, such as consensus, failover, exactly-once behavior, or other unforgiving systems properties.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.name: Production delivery record
features.description: The breadth and depth of hands-on responsibility the letter shows for shipping, maintaining, operating, or launching real production systems.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant professional tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant full-time software engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Requirement mapping
features.description: How explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background to the posting's stated requirements, responsibilities, or target role.

levels.descriptor: Leaves the reader to infer most of the match to the posting.
Mentions relevant experience but ties it only loosely to the role.
Directly connects several experiences or skills to stated requirements or responsibilities.
Explicitly walks through the posting match in a structured, requirement-aware way.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: How specifically and compellingly the letter explains why this exact role is a desired next step, beyond generic job interest.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in applying with little reason for this role in particular.
States interest in the role but with broad or familiar reasoning.
Gives a clear role-specific reason tied to security engineering, automation, or impact.
Articulates a distinctive and memorable rationale that tightly links prior experience to this exact mandate.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through reviews, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How clearly the letter understands the team's core mission as scaling security expertise and workflows through software, automation, and tooling.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The rigor or strength of formal security certifications or other external security credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security worldview
features.description: The applicant's articulated philosophy or intrinsic orientation about the purpose and practice of security engineering.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct experience building systems that automate vulnerability intake, triage, routing, prioritization, deduplication, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree to which spelling, grammar, proofreading, and surface-level mechanics support the letter's professionalism and credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors noticeably distract and undermine polish.
Several errors are present, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor errors are present.
The letter is clean and professional throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: A catch-all for remaining distinct dimensions that do not clearly recur enough as the same standalone construct to warrant their own canonical criterion.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.
